1800 GOT JUNK Pricing in Dallas: 2026 Breakdown

If you’re scrolling through Dallas Google results for “junk removal near me,” chances are you’ve already stumbled on 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Their bright orange trucks are hard to miss, but the real question on everyone’s mind is: how much will it actually cost in 2026? In this guide we’ll peel back the pricing layers, explain what you’re paying for, and share insider tips to keep your bill as low as possible.

Why 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Remains a Top Choice in Dallas

Since its launch in 1997, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? has built a reputation for transparent pricing, speedy service, and a “no‑questions‑asked” attitude toward junk. In Dallas, the service’s popularity stems from three core strengths:

  • Uniform pricing: Rates are based on volume, not weight, so you won’t be surprised by hidden pounds.
  • All‑inclusive service: Loading, hauling, disposal, and recycling are covered in one price.
  • Eco‑friendly disposal: The company aims to recycle or donate at least 60% of every load.

All of that convenience comes with a price tag, and the 2026 rates reflect both market inflation and the company’s commitment to sustainability.

How the Pricing Model Works in 2026

In Dallas, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? continues to charge by cubic yards—the space your junk occupies in the back of the truck. The company measures each load in 1‑cubic‑yard increments, rounding up to the nearest whole yard. Here’s the basic breakdown:

Base Rate per Cubic Yard

For 2026 the base rate in the Dallas metro area is $89 per cubic yard. This figure is the starting point for every job, whether you’re clearing out a single bedroom or an entire commercial warehouse.

Minimum Load Requirement

Every service call carries a minimum charge for a 2‑cubic‑yard load, which translates to $178. If you have less than two cubic yards of junk, the minimum still applies—but you’ll get the full benefit of a professional team handling the job.

Additional Fees You Might See

  • Heavy‑Item Surcharge: Items like concrete blocks, large appliances, or pallets over 200 lb may incur a $20‑$40 surcharge per item.
  • Travel Fee: Jobs outside the 30‑mile radius of downtown Dallas could attract a $15‑$30 travel fee.
  • Hazardous Material Fee: If you have items such as paint cans, batteries, or chemicals, the company will quote a separate disposal rate to comply with local regulations.

These add‑ons are clearly outlined before any work begins, so there are no surprise charges on your final invoice.

What 2026 Costs Look Like in Real‑World Scenarios

Below are common Dallas clean‑out projects with estimated total prices (including the base rate, minimum load, and typical add‑ons). All figures are rounded to the nearest dollar.

Residential Clean‑Outs

  • One‑Bedroom Apartment: 3 cubic yards → $267 (3 × $89) + $20 heavy‑item surcharge = $287
  • Two‑Bedroom Home (including a mattress and small sofa): 5 cubic yards → $445 + $40 heavy‑item surcharge = $485
  • Full House Turn‑over (average 12 cubic yards): $1,068 + $60 heavy‑item surcharge = $1,128

Commercial & Office Junk Removal

  • Small Office (4 cubic yards of old furniture & electronics): $356 + $30 travel fee = $386
  • Retail Store Renovation (15 cubic yards of shelving, drywall, and packaging): $1,335 + $80 heavy‑item surcharge = $1,415

Special Projects

  • Construction Debris (concrete, bricks, 8 cubic yards): $712 + $60 hazardous material fee = $772
  • Yard Clean‑Up (branches, mulch, 4 cubic yards): $356 (no extra fees) = $356

Remember, these are estimates. The final quote can vary by a few dollars based on exact item dimensions, location, and any extra services you request.

Seasonal Discounts & Promotions You Can’t Miss

1-800-GOT-JUNK? frequently rolls out city‑wide promotions, especially during peak moving seasons (spring and summer) and holiday periods. Here’s what Dallas residents typically see:

  • Spring Move‑Out Special: 10% off the total bill for bookings made between March 1–May 31.
  • Summer Referral Bonus: Refer a friend and both of you receive $30 off your next service.
  • Black Friday Flash Deal: Up to 15% off for bookings made on Black Friday weekend.

These offers are time‑sensitive, so it’s a good idea to ask the dispatcher about any current promotions before you lock in your appointment.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Do I pay for labor separately?

No. The per‑cubic‑yard rate includes the crew’s labor, loading, and disposal. The only extra charges are the optional fees listed earlier.

What items are not accepted?
